#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Copyright (c) 2021-2026 tteck
# Author: tteck (tteckster)
# License: MIT | https://github.com/community-scripts/ProxmoxVE/raw/main/LICENSE
# Source: https://uptime.kuma.pet/ | Github: https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma

source /dev/stdin <<<"$FUNCTIONS_FILE_PATH"
color
verb_ip6
catch_errors
setting_up_container
network_check
update_os

msg_info "Installing dependencies"
$STD apt install -y chromium
msg_ok "Installed dependencies"

NODE_VERSION="22" setup_nodejs
fetch_and_deploy_gh_release "uptime-kuma" "louislam/uptime-kuma" "tarball"

msg_info "Installing Uptime Kuma"
cd /opt/uptime-kuma
$STD npm ci --omit dev
$STD npm run download-dist
msg_ok "Installed Uptime Kuma"

msg_info "Creating Service"
ln -s /usr/bin/chromium /opt/uptime-kuma/chromium
cat <<EOF >/etc/systemd/system/uptime-kuma.service
[Unit]
Description=uptime-kuma

[Service]
Type=simple
Restart=always
User=root
WorkingDirectory=/opt/uptime-kuma
ExecStart=/usr/bin/npm start

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
systemctl enable -q --now uptime-kuma
msg_ok "Created Service"

motd_ssh
customize
cleanup_lxc

I wrote the decision file to `.agent/uptimekuma/research.json`. I only read the upstream install script and checked the package and module options. I didn't read `ct/uptimekuma.sh`, and I didn't evaluate or build anything.

- **Approach:** `extracted`. nixpkgs has `uptime-kuma` (version 2.5.5) and a `services.uptime-kuma` module. I didn't check whether a modular service exists, so `modular_service` is `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - **Unit:** `uptime-kuma`.
  - **Port:** 3001.
  - **Data directory:** `/var/lib/uptime-kuma`.
  - **Env vars:** `HOST`, `PORT`, `DATA_DIR` and the optional MariaDB settings (`UPTIME_KUMA_DB_*`). The module sets them through `services.uptime-kuma.settings`.
- **Healthcheck:** `/api/entry-page` on port 3001. I picked it from memory and haven't confirmed it returns 2xx without login. `/` may redirect instead.
- **Listen address:** I recorded `HOST` as `0.0.0.0` but didn't check the module's default. The author needs to set it explicitly.
- **Setup:** the admin account is created in the web UI on first visit. The default SQLite database needs nothing else.
- **Upstream differences:** upstream installs Node 22 and a release tarball under `/opt/uptime-kuma` and runs it as root. We use the nixpkgs package and module instead. Upstream also installs Chromium (for browser-engine monitors). I didn't work out how to provide it in the NixOS service, so the notes only mention it as optional.
